record: issue-77 single-corner diagnosis probe 4: R15 start-up at the 3.6 ohm load, kelvin control return + 100 MHz single-pole EA stand-in (simulated, pre-layout; NOT measured)
corner: typical / Vin 5.0 V / 27 C / 3.6 ohm resistor on out from t=0; Vin ramps 0->5 V over 10 us, EN at 20 us

run.change_vs_probe3: Iload (0 until 260 us) replaced by a 3.6 ohm resistor from t=0, so the start-up is under load
run.steady_state: not established as a spec 0.4 settled test; 40 us window means of Vout are 1.692 V from 260 us to 700 us

observations.t_90: 181.8 us after EN (threshold 1.62 V on the per-cycle mean), inside the R15 window 100-500 us
observations.peak_il: 0.571 A during start-up, below the 0.70 A R16 minimum trip
observations.monotonic: FALSE by the 1 mV tolerance: max drawdown 18.9 mV (probe3, no load: 20.7 mV), cause not traced
observations.final_vout: 1.692 V from 260 us, 6 percent below 1.8 V (no load: 1.773 V); vc-gnd_d keeps ramping 1.74 -> 3.20 V (rail) between 220 and 580 us, then sits at the rail while Vout does not move. Cause not traced (candidates, none tested: duty headroom limit, switch Ron drop, finite EA stand-in gain)

diagnosis: PARTIAL. At this corner under load the unit starts up (t_90 inside the window, peak current below the R16 min trip), so the earlier failures are not an oscillator, bias or soft-start-reference fault here either. Two things still fail with the stand-in EA and kelvin control return: the monotonic clause (18.9 mV drawdown) and a 6 percent Vout shortfall at 3.6 ohm with vc pinned at the 3.3 V rail. The shortfall is a candidate design defect (control authority runs out) but is NOT traced, so no decision record is written. No spec row, design netlist or earlier record is changed.
not_done: monotonic drawdown node trace; a second (originally failing) corner; R16 trip probe; the 6 percent shortfall cause; the grid (#60)
